lesson_title: The General Journal: Fixing Mistakes in Pen
hook_text: Real bookkeepers NEVER erase. Here's why a visible mistake is worth more than a perfect page.
clip_script: What it never does: erase, tippex, tear out the page. Not because neatness matters, but because trust does. A book where numbers can quietly change is a book that proves nothing — not to the owner, not to the bank, not to anyone. So mistakes are fixed in pen, with a new entry that reverses exactly the broken piece, and the sentence underneath: correction of error. The wrong entry stays visible; the correction stands beside it, dated and explained. That is called an audit trail — and nobody believes perfect books; everybody believes books that show their own repairs.
visual_style: A hand hovering with correction fluid over a ledger — frozen, rejected — then writing a clean correcting entry below in ink, both entries glowing side by side with a 'TRUSTED' stamp.
pacing: Tense hover on the tippex moment, firm rule drop, warm resolution on the audit trail.
